title: What a shopper's browser loads
headline: A shopper's first page is mostly well kept, and nothing here argues for removing a feature: a cold home page sends 680 KB of scripts (213 KB gzip), 63 % of it React and Next, with no third-party script and no font file. What is left is cost that does not follow use and that grows with page views once stores open. On a default store every document load makes two extra function calls (a wishlist read that is nearly always empty and, on pages with a product grid, a stock read for tiles that show nothing), carries about 48 KB raw / 16 KB gzip of admin words, catalogues and one unused library in its first scripts, and sends the store's layout twice (25 KB) with the store's 404 page inside. Eleven working routes share one 54-module bundle (30 KB gzip more than a built page), stores with several languages prefetch 70 to 105 KB of views a press never opens, and a store in an AI-translated language would send its whole interface text, about 100 KB, in every page. Thirteen findings: six are small and safe (P0); the two that move route files (per-route bundles, the drawer's slot) are cheapest before opening; the budgets that should have caught the growth have about 150 KB of room and cover two storefront routes.

clean: No large object crosses into client components in the four hand-written languages: the inline payloads of the home, product, category and cart pages hold none of the Store's fields; props are small labels and ids. A product grid's tile words are sent once and referenced by the other tiles. The exception is an AI-translated language (SC-13).

The extras are server-gated and lazy: chat widget, consent manager, owner's code, referral capture, country hint and first-visit keeper are drawn only when the store has them (src/app/s/[store]/[market]/extras.tsx, src/components/lazy/extras.tsx) and load as their own chunks, the chat and referral capture only when idle. A store pays for these only when it uses them.
Motion runtime: a 702-byte stub; the runtime is a dynamic import. The 3D viewer loads only on a press. web-vitals is a dynamic import.
Visit and speed beacons are drawn only while the owner has visit counting on (src/components/store-visits.tsx:12), off by default. Once on, each page view sends a beacon: that cost follows use.

No third-party script, font file or beacon on a storefront page by default: 0 third-party requests and 0 font files on the 12 measured pages. A store's own fonts are one stylesheet a family, kept for a year, with the Latin file preloaded (src/components/font-links.tsx, font-preloads.tsx); not measured here because the demo store uses none.
zod, the page model and whole-language texts stay out of the visitor's scripts (src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts:16, e2e/performance.spec.ts:27).

Product tiles in content grids are plain anchors, never prefetched (src/components/content-grid.tsx). The language switcher part (LanguageLinks) draws plain anchors too, so it never prefetches (src/components/language-links.tsx:84).
Language, currency and country links exist only in stores that offer more than one (src/components/store-layout.tsx:173, 224), so their prefetch cost (SC-1) falls only on those stores.

Features with empty tables in production (A/B tests, reviews, gift cards, AI-translated interface texts, 3D) are not findings: the platform has not opened. Where their client code is lazy and server-gated, a store that does not use them pays nothing. Where it is not, the finding is about the idle cost or the size, never about the feature.

Weighed and left: the browser texts of all four languages load together (24,831 raw / about 7.2 KB gzip). docs/performance.md:52-60 (D212) records that a per-language load made the page wait and lost presses.

Weighed and left: filter-dialog (11,773 raw), site-form (6,348) and carousel (6,712) are in every built page's first scripts; the written rule keeps what is pressed before its script runs (docs/performance.md:38-51).

Weighed and left: back-to-admin, admin-return and page-edit-link run on every page by design: the browser, not the server, decides whether the visitor is staff, so the page stays cached for all (src/components/back-to-admin.tsx:31-38).

findings.title: Every document load prefetches the pages behind its links; language and currency links prefetch a page a press never opens
findings.evidence: Re-tallied from m/routes.json per target (phone, cold cache). Home: 11 RSC prefetches, 32,830 bytes: search 3 / 8,301, wishlist 3 / 8,258, cart 3 / 10,576, account 2 / 5,695. Content page /om-oss: 34 prefetches, 143,036 bytes, of which the four views no-sv, no-da, no-en and no-sek take 12 requests and 70,459 bytes, the footer's cookies link 2 / 6,450 and its withdrawal link 2 / 5,675. Empty cart: 42 prefetches, 184,408 bytes, of which six views take 18 requests and 104,635 bytes. Each view is 3 requests and about 85,000 decoded bytes because another view is the whole layout again. The view links are ViewMenu's Link (view-menu.tsx:56), which the standard footer draws as a list (store-layout.tsx:531) and the phone menu too. Its click handler calls preventDefault and pushes the page the shopper is on (view-menu.tsx:62-72), so the prefetched front page is what a press opens only from the front page. Correction to the verified report: LanguageLinks is not a source. It draws plain anchors (language-links.tsx:84), which are never prefetched. Next's reference (link.md:302-304): the default prefetches the full route for a static route; prefetch={false} never prefetches, on view or on hover. next.config.ts does not set partialPrefetching. The prefetch answers carry s-maxage, so they are cached shells, not page renders. Not measured: the countries list (three Links, store-layout.tsx:236, 419, 537 and site-parts.tsx:191), because the demo store sells in one country; each country is another view like a language. Listing cards are Links as well (product-card.tsx:74): the one product link the demo's category shows cost 2 requests and 7,874 bytes.
findings.cost: Per cold document load, not per client-side move. Stores with several languages or currencies: 17.3 to 17.7 KB and 3 requests for each such link in view (70 KB for four, 105 KB for six). Every store: 12 KB and 4 requests for the footer's cookies and withdrawal links when the footer is in view, and 33 KB for the header's four tools. The answers are fetched again on each document load; content-grid tiles and every entry into the cart or checkout are document loads, so one visit pays several times.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser (data, battery). The edge and proxy.ts once per prefetch request. Not a page render: the answers are cached shells.

findings.title: A store in a language translated by AI sends its whole interface text in every page; the browser reads 114 of its 1,673 texts
findings.evidence: Read in code in this pass. The market layout hands the client component UiTexts whatever uiTextsFor(market.lang) returns (layout.tsx:131, 160). For a language without hand-written text that is every 'ui:' text of the language: loadLanguage() keeps all rows whose key does not start with 'email:' (ui-text.ts:48-53) and uiTextsFor() returns that map (ui-text.ts:127-129). A prop of a client component is written into the page's inline payload, so every page of such a store carries it. In the browser it is laid over browserText('en') only (ui-texts.tsx:21, browser-text.ts:16-18); the one other reader is the withdrawal page (returns-text.ts:19-20, withdraw-flow.tsx:57). Measured from the real catalogue with English as the stand-in (work/plan-sc/catalog-size.cjs runs catalogOf() of src/lib/ui-catalog.ts on the message files): the whole catalogue is 1,673 texts, 92,919 bytes of JSON, 99,613 bytes as written in the HTML, 25,416 gzip. The browser's texts are 114 texts, 5,862 bytes, 1,886 gzip. The withdrawal function's are 144 texts, 10,411 bytes. The home document is 138,410 bytes / 18,691 gzip today. docs/performance.md:52-60 (D212) states the rule this breaks: a visitor's browser gets only the texts its client components read. For nb, sv, da and en the prop is null and nothing is sent. Not run in a browser: the seed has no translated language, so the sizes are an estimate from the catalogue.
findings.cost: About 100 KB raw / 25 KB gzip more in every document of a store whose language is not nb, sv, da or en: the home document would be about 1.7 times its size raw and more than twice compressed. The same in every prefetch answer that carries the layout. Nothing for stores in the four hand-written languages. The cost falls only on stores that use the feature, but it is sixteen times what they need, on every page view, and Kaizena Flow sells EU-wide, where most languages go through this path.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser (download and parse on every page); the server per request (it serialises the map each time)
